title: Comparing Explanations is Not Enough, Explain the Change: New Standards are Needed to Explain Behavioral Shifts in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2602.02304v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large-scale foundation models exhibit behavioral shifts when subjected to interventions such as scaling, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning with human feedback, or in-context learning. Current explainability methods are structurally ill-suited to explain these shifts, because they either treat models as static objects, as traditional eXplainable AI (XAI) approaches do, or merely compare independent explanations across different checkpoints of a model. As a result, these approaches fail to explain the functional transition between two model instances in which a certain behavior has shifted following an intervention. This gap creates significant governance risks across jurisdictions including the EU AI Act, US state legislation, and Chinese AI regulations, which require documenting causal chains for substantial system modifications. translated_title: 比较解释并不足够，要解释变化：需要新标准来解释大型语言模型中的行为转变
translated_abstract: 摘要：大规模基础模型在经历扩展、微调、基于人类反馈的强化学习或上下文学习等干预时，会表现出行为转变。当前的可解释性方法在结构上不适合解释这些转变，因为它们要么像传统可解释人工智能（XAI）方法那样将模型视为静态对象，要么仅仅比较模型不同检查点之间的独立解释。因此，这些方法无法解释两个模型实例之间的功能转换，其中某种行为在干预后发生了改变。这一差距在多个司法管辖区（包括欧盟人工智能法案、美国州立法和中国人工智能法规）中造成了重大治理风险，这些法规要求对实质性系统修改记录因果链。本立场论文认为，解释大型语言模型中的行为转变需要一种原则性的方法。
tldr: 本文提出，当前可解释性方法无法充分解释大型语言模型在干预后的行为转变，并呼吁建立新标准以满足治理要求。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that current explainability methods fail to adequately explain behavioral shifts in large language models after interventions, and calls for new standards to meet governance requirements.
